chapter: Family and early memories of Jelly
title: Jelly sent to Biloxi to avoid the shady places
summary: Grandmother worried about children and disease, so relatives cared for Jelly until he left for Biloxi and beyond the Mason-Dixon line.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Your brother left home, your grandmother didn't get along with him, I think you said, or he said that

Well, I mean, she just didn't approve of him working in these shady places And coming back home where the children were She was so afraid of the narrow diseases, that's why she didn't want to become And you see, she had a sister that lived next door to his guard mother And her sister was my sister's guard mother So I mean, they took good care of him until he got ready to travel And go on the other side of the line, Mason-Dixon line, you know what I mean?
So he went over to Biloxi then?

He went over to Biloxi until I think he was maybe seventeen or nineteen, something like twenty or something I don't know, I don't know how old he was But I mean the last time I saw him, the first time I ever saw him, to remember him He was in Biloxi with my aunt, Hortense was her name Hortense? Yeah, they called Hortense H-O-R?
